pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: Oranges and Lemons
work.note: Oranges and Lemons é uma rima infantil tradicional inglesa, registrada por volta de 1744. Os versos fazem referência a igrejas de Londres, cujos sinos parecem cantar um após o outro. A rima também é um jogo de roda, e termina com uma contagem. Ela é muito ligada à cidade de Londres e a seus sinos. A referência abre a situação para praticar “pedir pela medida com a pound of e a dozen, como no mercado de laranjas e lim

pages.title: Fruit day in Miami · 1/3
paragraphs: Today I went to a fruit stand in **Miami**. The sun was hot and the fruit looked great. A man smiled and said, “Good morning! Can I help you?”
I asked, “**How much are** the mangoes?” He said, “**They’re two dollars each**.” I said, “**I’ll take four**, please.” Four mangoes cost eight dollars. That was a **good deal**!
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Fruit day in Miami · 2/3
paragraphs: Then I asked, “**Do you have** bananas?” “**Sure!**” he said. “**They’re one dollar a pound**.” I wanted **two pounds**. A pound is a little less than half a kilo, so I was not sure about the size. But the bananas were nice.
The man put the fruit on the **scale**. “**That’s ten dollars**,” he said. Eight dollars for the mangoes and two for the bananas. I gave him a ten-dollar bill and said, “Here you go. Thank you!”

pages.title: Fruit day in Miami · 3/3
paragraphs: On the way home, I remembered an old English rhyme: “Oranges and lemons, say the bells.” At a market in London, a seller says, “**A pound of oranges, please.**” Fruit stands are a little like a small song.
Tonight I will eat a mango. It is sweet, and it makes me happy. Tomorrow I want to buy tomatoes and an onion!
